mainTopic: Why the משנה lists four ראשי השנים, the source of the dispute over the New Year for מעשר בהמה, and what 'the first of תשרי is ראש השנה for years' means: documents, the תקופה, or judgment
overview: This amud first finishes the question of why the משנה counts only four ראשי השנים. The גמרא defends the rule about יובל by saying the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. רב אשי then gives another answer: the משנה lists the New Years that fall on a ראש חודש, with the first of שבט being part of the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל. Next, רבי יוחנן says רבי מאיר (אלול) and רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון (תשרי) argue about מעשר בהמה based on one פסוק in תהלים about when sheep conceive. The order of that פסוק fits only רבי מאיר, so רבא moves the argument to ״עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר״, a היקש between מעשר בהמה and מעשר דגן that each side reads differently. The גמרא then asks what 'the first of תשרי is ראש השנה for years' is for. Three answers are given: dating documents (רב פפא, with ניסן for Jewish kings and תשרי for non-Jewish kings), the solar cycles (רבי זירא), and the day of judgment (רב נחמן בר יצחק). The amud ends as the גמרא begins proving from the שופר פסוק in תהלים that the judgment is in תשרי, a proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from the Jubilee Year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that the משנה leaves out New Years that depend on an action. יובל seems to depend on blowing the שופר, yet the משנה counts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the Jubilee Years? (They depend on an action, and the משנה still counts them!)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave by pointing to יובל, which the משנה does count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer said the משנה lists no New Year that depends on an action. But a יובל year normally takes effect only when the שופר is blown on יום הכיפורים, which is an action. So listing יובל seems to break the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, there is... (a word that opens a challenge)
Jubilee Years, every fiftieth year
Something that depends on an action (the principle being challenged)

steps.confusionAlert: The two words 'והרי יובלות' are a whole question. The rest of the challenge is implied: 'יובל depends on the שופר, so why is it counted?'

phrases.english: But there are the Jubilee Years!
phrases.notes: The point is that יובל depends on blowing the שופר, yet the משנה still lists it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier answer (on the previous amud) that the משנה leaves out New Years that depend on an action.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that the תנא does not count a New Year that depends on an action
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יובל depends on blowing the שופר, which is an action, yet the משנה counts its New Year.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. In his view, יובל starts on ראש השנה on its own, without depending on the שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This משנה follows the opinion of רבי ישמעאל, the son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its rule by saying the משנה follows a תנא for whom יובל does not depend on any action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה holds that the יובל year begins on ראש השנה of the fiftieth year even before the שופר is blown. For him, יובל is not a 'depends on an action' New Year. So the rule still holds, and listing יובל is no problem.

keyTerms.term: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds that יובל begins on ראש השנה
It is (the משנה follows this view)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, the son of
Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, is the author (of the Mishnah).
phrases.notes: He holds יובל starts at ראש השנה, independent of the שופר.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from יובל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the anonymous משנה is assigned to a specific תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יובל depends on the שופר, so counting it contradicts the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: For this תנא, יובל begins on ראש השנה itself, so it does not depend on an action and the rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: First answer to 'why only four?': the משנה skips New Years that depend on an action, and יובל is not one of them, because the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

steps.title: רב אשי: four New Years that fall on the first of a month
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different reason why the משנה lists only four. It counts only the New Years that fall on ראש חודש, the first day of a month.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The משנה means there are four New Years that fall on four ראשי חדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, separate answer to the original question of why the משנה says 'four' when other New Years exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of the 'depends on an action' rule, רב אשי reads the number four as limited: four New Years that start on the first of a month. Other New Years exist, but they do not start on ראש חודש, so the משנה did not count them.

keyTerms.meaning: First days of the month (New Moons)

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi said:
There are four New Years
that fall on four New Moons (first days of months).
phrases.notes: This hints that there are other New Years that don't fall on the first of a month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the original question, independent of the 'depends on an action' rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of the number in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Four' seems to mean these are the only New Years.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Four' means four New Years that fall on ראש חודש. Others exist but are not counted.

steps.title: Challenge: does the first of שבט follow בית שמאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי. The first of שבט is the New Year for trees only according to בית שמאי, and the הלכה follows בית הלל, who say ט״ו בשבט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first of שבט — is that like בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how רב אשי can count the first of שבט as one of the four New Years on a ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית שמאי say the New Year for trees is the first of שבט, while בית הלל say the fifteenth. Since we follow בית הלל, the trees' New Year is not on a ראש חודש. So it seems רב אשי has only three New Years on a first of the month.

keyTerms.meaning: On the first of שבט
The school of שמאי, usually not followed in הלכה
The school of הלל, whose view is the הלכה

phrases.english: The first of Shevat — is that according to Beit Shammai?
phrases.notes: בית הלל say ט״ו בשבט, and the הלכה follows them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's count of four New Years on ראש חודש.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that four New Years fall on a first of the month
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The New Year for trees is on the first of שבט only for בית שמאי. Under בית הלל, which is the הלכה, it is on the fifteenth, so only three fall on a first of the month.

steps.title: Three agreed by all, and שבט is disputed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רב אשי's meaning. Three New Years fall on ראש חודש according to everyone, and the first of שבט is part of the מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: three are on the first of the month according to everyone, and the first of שבט is the subject of a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies רב אשי's statement so he no longer seems to follow בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי is not ruling like בית שמאי. He is describing the משנה as it stands: three New Years are on the first of a month according to everyone, and a fourth, the first of שבט, is on the first of a month according to one side of a dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (a clarifying reinterpretation)
According to everyone
A dispute

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
Three (fall on the first of the month) according to everyone,

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶחָד בִּשְׁבָט — מַחְלוֹקֶת בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל.
phrases.english: and the first of Shevat is a dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about שבט by reinterpreting רב אשי's words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation (הכי קאמר) of the earlier statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אשי counts the first of שבט as a settled ראש חודש New Year, which would mean he follows בית שמאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three are on a first of the month according to everyone. The fourth is included only as one side of the בית שמאי and בית הלל dispute.
steps.whatToRemember: Second answer to 'why only four?' (רב אשי): the משנה counts New Years that fall on a ראש חודש. Three are agreed by all, and the first of שבט is disputed.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: both sides learned from one verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's view of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון that the New Year for מעשר בהמה is the first of תשרי. רבי יוחנן says both they and רבי מאיר learned their views from one פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון hold it is on the first of תשרי. רבי יוחנן said: Both of them learned from the same פסוק, as it says, 'The flocks are clothed in the meadows, and the valleys are wrapped in grain; they shout for joy, they also sing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic, the dispute about the New Year for animal tithes. It sets up the verse that both sides will read in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר says the New Year for מעשר בהמה is the first of אלול, and רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say the first of תשרי. רבי יוחנן claims the disagreement is not about different sources. Both read the same פסוק in תהלים, but they understand its timing differently. The next steps explain each reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The tithe of animals, every tenth animal born in a year
They interpreted one verse
Rams, or meadows (both meanings are used here)
Wrapped (covered) in grain

steps.confusionAlert: Even though only רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון are quoted, 'שניהם' (both of them) means רבי מאיר on one side and רבי אלעזר on the other.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה about מעשר בהמה.

phrases.english: (it is) on the first of Tishrei.
Rabbi Yochanan said:
And both of them expounded the same verse,
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: as it is stated: “The flocks are clothed in the meadows (by the rams),
phrases.notes: תהלים סה:יד

phrases.english: and the valleys are wrapped in grain;
they shout for joy, they also sing.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה: the New Year for מעשר בהמה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר (first of אלול) and רבי אלעזר (first of תשרי) both derive their views from the same פסוק in תהלים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the dispute is about how to read the verse's timing, not about which source to use. Each reading will set a different date for counting animals for the tithe.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's reading leads to אלול
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר reads the verse as linking the time sheep conceive to the time grain covers the valleys, which is אדר. The sheep give birth five months later in אב, so their New Year is the first of אלול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: When are the flocks 'clothed' by the rams? At the time when the valleys are covered with grain. And when are the valleys covered with grain? In אדר. The sheep conceive in אדר and give birth in אב, so their New Year is אלול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי מאיר gets the first of אלול out of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads the two halves of the verse as happening at the same time: the sheep are 'clothed' (mated) when the grain covers the valleys, in אדר. Five months later, in אב, the lambs are born. So the new 'crop' of animals is complete by the end of אב, and the tithe year starts on the first of אלול. רבי אלעזר's reading comes next in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
They conceive (become pregnant)
They give birth

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: grain covers the valleys in אדר, so sheep conceive in אדר, give birth in אב, and the New Year for מעשר בהמה is the first of אלול.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
When are the flocks 'clothed' by the rams?
phrases.notes: When the rams mate with the ewes.

phrases.english: At the time when the valleys are wrapped in grain.
And when are the valleys wrapped in grain? In Adar.
They conceive in Adar and give birth in Av,
phrases.notes: Five months of pregnancy for sheep.

phrases.english: so their New Year is (the first of) Elul.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר אֵימָתַי לָבְשׁוּ כָרִים הַצֹּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the two readings of the verse that רבי יוחנן brought.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sheep conceive in אדר when grain covers the valleys and give birth in אב, so the New Year for מעשר בהמה is the first of אלול.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון read the verse as pointing to ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say the sheep conceive when the grain 'sings' in ניסן. They give birth in אלול, so their New Year is תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say: When are 'the meadows clothed with flocks'? At the time when 'they shout for joy, they also sing.' When do the grain stalks 'sing'? In ניסן. So the sheep conceive in ניסן and give birth in אלול, and their New Year is תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second reading of the same verse, the one used by רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון. It parallels רבי מאיר's reading from Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר tied the sheep's conceiving to the first half of the verse, 'the valleys are wrapped in grain,' which is אדר. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון tie it to the second half, 'they shout for joy and sing.' That means full stalks rustling in the wind in ניסן. Five months later is אלול, so the counting year for the newborn animals starts right after, on א׳ תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The meadows are clothed with flocks', meaning the sheep conceive (literally, they are 'dressed' with pregnancy)
'They shout for joy, they also sing', the second half of the verse
Stalks or ears of grain
They conceive / become pregnant

steps.confusionAlert: The 'singing' is not about people singing. It describes the full grain stalks rustling in the wind, which happens in ניסן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
When are 'the meadows clothed with flocks'?
phrases.notes: The time the sheep conceive.

phrases.english: At the time when 'they shout for joy, they also sing.'
When do the grain stalks sing? In Nisan.
phrases.notes: The full stalks rustle in the wind.

phrases.english: They conceive in Nisan and give birth in Elul,
so their New Year is Tishrei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading of the same verse that רבי מאיר used in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sheep conceive in ניסן and give birth in אלול, so the New Year for מעשר בהמה is א׳ תשרי.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי מאיר from the second half of the verse
steps.stepSummary: If רבי מאיר says the sheep conceive in אדר, what does he do with the words 'they shout for joy and sing,' which point to ניסן?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the other one, רבי מאיר, too: isn't it written 'they shout for joy, they also sing'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks רבי מאיר what he does with the half of the verse that רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse mentions two times: אדר (valleys wrapped in grain) and ניסן (stalks singing). רבי מאיר only used the אדר part. So the גמרא asks what the ניסן part is there for in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, meaning the other opinion
But isn't it written…? (introduces a verse used as a challenge)

phrases.english: And the other one too,
phrases.notes: Referring to רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: isn't it written: 'They shout for joy, they also sing'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי מאיר's reading (Step 7) using the half of the verse that Step 8 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's reading that the sheep conceive in אדר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse also mentions the ניסן season. If the sheep conceive in אדר, that phrase seems unexplained.

steps.title: The ניסן phrase refers to late sheep
steps.stepSummary: For רבי מאיר, 'they shout for joy and sing' describes late sheep, which conceive in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase is about the late sheep, which conceive in ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי מאיר. Both halves of the verse are true, but the second half describes a smaller group of late sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most sheep conceive in אדר, and that sets their New Year (אלול). Some sheep conceive late, in ניסן, and the second half of the verse refers to them. So nothing in the verse is left unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: Late ones: sheep that conceive later than usual

phrases.english: That refers to the late ones, which conceive in Nisan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the verse: each half describes a different group of sheep.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ניסן phrase seemed to contradict רבי מאיר's אדר reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר, the ניסן phrase describes only the minority of late sheep.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון from the first half of the verse
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say the sheep conceive in ניסן, what do they do with 'the valleys are wrapped in grain,' which points to אדר?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the other ones, רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, too: isn't it written 'and the valleys are wrapped in grain'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same question in reverse. What do רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון do with the אדר half of the verse?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors Step 9. Each side seems to ignore one half of the verse, so each side has to explain the half it did not use.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the valleys are wrapped in grain', the first half of the verse (אדר)

phrases.english: And the other ones too,
phrases.notes: Referring to רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: isn't it written: 'And the valleys are wrapped in grain'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror-image challenge to Step 9, now aimed at רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון's reading that the sheep conceive in ניסן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse also mentions the אדר season. If the sheep conceive in ניסן, that phrase seems unexplained.

steps.title: The אדר phrase refers to early sheep
steps.stepSummary: For רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, 'the valleys are wrapped in grain' describes early sheep, which conceive in אדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase is about the early sheep, which conceive in אדר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון the same way it answered for רבי מאיר. The other half of the verse describes a minority group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In their view, most sheep conceive in ניסן, and some early ones conceive in אדר. So each opinion now accounts for the whole verse. They only disagree about which half describes the main group.

keyTerms.meaning: Early ones: sheep that conceive earlier than usual

phrases.english: That refers to the early ones, which conceive in Adar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the verse: each half describes a different group of sheep.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אדר phrase seemed to contradict their ניסן reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, the אדר phrase describes only the minority of early sheep.

steps.title: The order of the verse fits only רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The verse first says 'valleys wrapped in grain' and then 'they sing.' That order fits רבי מאיר, but רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון would need the reverse order.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבי מאיר: as written, the sheep conceive when the valleys are wrapped in grain, and there are also some at the time of 'they shout for joy and sing.' But for רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, the verse should have been written in the reverse order: the sheep conceive at the time of 'they shout for joy and sing,' and there are also some when 'the valleys are wrapped in grain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a stronger challenge against רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, based on the order of the words in the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse should mention the main time first and the minority time second. It mentions אדר first, which matches רבי מאיר, who holds most sheep conceive in אדר. For רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, who hold most conceive in ניסן, the verse is in the wrong order. This problem is what pushes the גמרא to a new approach in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for… (sets up a contrast: this view is fine, but the other is difficult)
It should have been the reverse
And there are also (some others)

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge is never answered directly. Instead it causes רבא to reject the whole idea that the מחלוקת depends on this verse.

phrases.english: It works well for Rabbi Meir,
as it is written: 'The meadows are clothed with flocks'
at the time when 'the valleys are wrapped in grain,'
phrases.notes: The main time, אדר, comes first.

phrases.english: and there are also some at 'they shout for joy, they also sing.'
phrases.notes: The minority, ניסן, comes second.

phrases.english: But for Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon,
it should have been the reverse:
'The meadows are clothed with flocks'
at the time when 'they shout for joy, they also sing,'
and there are also some when 'the valleys are wrapped in grain.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Even after Steps 10 and 12 explain both halves, the order of the verse still works only for רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון's use of the verse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse lists the main case first. The verse lists אדר first, so it supports רבי מאיר and reads backwards for רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבא says everyone agrees about אדר and the argument is about a different verse
steps.stepSummary: רבא says all agree the sheep mainly conceive in אדר. The מחלוקת is really about ״עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר״, which speaks of two tithes, מעשר בהמה and מעשר דגן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Everyone agrees that the sheep conceive when the valleys are wrapped in grain, in אדר. Here they argue about this verse: 'You shall surely tithe.' The verse speaks about two tithes, one the animal tithe and the other the grain tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops the earlier approach and gives a new source for the מחלוקת. This step sets up the next move: the גמרא will next explain how this verse leads each side to its date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows the earlier explanation is being rejected because of Step 13. Now there is no argument about nature: all agree the sheep conceive in אדר. The disagreement moves to ״עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר״, a doubled phrase that hints at two tithes, animals and grain, being taught together. The link between them will determine each side's New Year.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
They disagree
'You shall surely tithe' (דברים יד:כב), a doubled verb
Animal tithe: every tenth newborn animal
Grain tithe

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not adding to the earlier explanation. He replaces it. In his view, רבי מאיר and רבי אלעזר ורבי שמעון do not argue about when sheep conceive at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the whole basis of the מחלוקת. It moves from a reading about nature in תהילים to a link between two tithes in the תורה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Everyone agrees that 'the meadows are clothed with flocks'
at the time when 'the valleys are wrapped in grain,' in Adar,
and here they disagree about this verse:
'You shall surely tithe'
the verse speaks about two tithes:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה וְאֶחָד מַעֲשֵׂר דָּגָן.
phrases.english: one the animal tithe and one the grain tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the unanswered challenge of Step 13 by replacing the whole approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the earlier approach: the מחלוקת is moved to a different verse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the מחלוקת depended on when sheep conceive, based on the verse in תהילים.
steps.terutzMaskana: All agree the sheep conceive in אדר. The מחלוקת depends on how ״עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר״ links מעשר בהמה to מעשר דגן.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: Animal tithe is taken right after the animals are complete, like grain
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי מאיר reads the היקש as comparing the timing of the two tithes. Grain is tithed close to when it is finished, so animals are also tithed close to when they are finished being born.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds that the verse compares animal tithe to grain tithe. Grain tithe is separated close to when the grain is finished, so animal tithe is also separated close to when the animals are finished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רבא's answer and explains what רבי מאיר learns from the comparison of the two tithes in ״עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that the verse links מעשר בהמה with מעשר דגן. רבי מאיר takes the link to be about timing: you tithe soon after the produce is complete. Grain finishes in אלול and is tithed in תשרי. Animals are born by אב, so their tithe year starts in אלול.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse compares (makes a היקש between) two things, so the law of one applies to the other
Animal tithe: every tenth newborn animal is set aside
Grain tithe
Close to its completion
Its tithing

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier pesukim about sheep. רבא has just said that everyone agrees about when the sheep conceive. The real argument is only about how to read the היקש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
The verse compares animal tithe to grain tithe:
phrases.notes: This comes from ״עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר״ (Step 14).

phrases.aramaic: מָה מַעֲשֵׂר דָּגָן — סָמוּךְ לִגְמָרוֹ עִישּׂוּרוֹ,
phrases.english: Just as grain tithe is separated close to the grain's completion,
phrases.notes: Grain is finished in אלול and tithed in תשרי.

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה — סָמוּךְ לִגְמָרוֹ עִישּׂוּרוֹ.
phrases.english: so too animal tithe is separated close to the animals' completion.
phrases.notes: Animals are born by אב, so their tithe year begins in אלול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of רבא's claim that the argument is really about ״עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר״.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the source of the argument from the sheep pesukim to how each side reads the היקש
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that the argument depended on when the sheep conceive.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר reads the היקש as being about timing: tithe soon after completion, so the ראש השנה for animal tithe is אלול.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון: Animal tithe shares grain's New Year in תשרי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון read the same היקש as comparing the New Year dates. Grain tithe's year starts in תשרי, so animal tithe's year starts in תשרי too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון hold that the verse compares animal tithe to grain tithe. Grain tithe's New Year is in תשרי, so animal tithe's New Year is also in תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of רבא's answer and shows how רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון use the same comparison differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides learn from the same verse. They disagree only about what part of grain tithe carries over to animal tithe. רבי מאיר says it is the timing (close to completion). רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say it is the actual date (תשרי).

keyTerms.meaning: They hold (plural)
The month of תשרי, the New Year for grain tithe

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees there is a היקש between מעשר בהמה and מעשר דגן. רבי מאיר compares the timing, which gives אלול. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון compare the date, which gives תשרי.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon hold:
The verse compares animal tithe to grain tithe:

phrases.aramaic: מָה מַעֲשֵׂר דָּגָן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁלּוֹ תִּשְׁרִי —
phrases.english: just as grain tithe's New Year is in Tishrei,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁלּוֹ תִּשְׁרִי.
phrases.english: so too animal tithe's New Year is in Tishrei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer by giving the second reading of the same היקש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same verse, different point of comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון seemed to depend on a sheep verse whose order of words did not fit their view.
steps.terutzMaskana: They learn תשרי directly from the היקש to grain tithe.

steps.title: What practical law comes from תשרי being the New Year for years?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, 'On the first of תשרי is ראש השנה for years,' and asks what practical law this teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the first of תשרי is ראש השנה for years. For what law does this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks what it is for, which sets up the answer that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying that a year 'starts' on some date only means something if a law depends on it. The גמרא wants to know which law makes counting years from תשרי matter.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Year for counting years
For what law (does this matter)?

phrases.english: On the first of Tishrei is the New Year for years.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: For what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of מעשר בהמה and starts discussing the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which practical law depends on years starting in תשרי.

steps.title: רב פפא: It is for dating loan documents
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says this rule is for dating documents (שטרות). A loan document with a date that is too early is invalid, and one with a date that is too late is valid. So we must know when the year changes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is for documents. As we learned: loan documents dated too early are invalid, and those dated too late are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. Counting years from תשרי matters for writing the correct date on documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A document dated earlier than the real loan is invalid. The lender could use that false early date to take back land the borrower sold before the loan actually happened. A document dated later is harmless, because it only hurts the lender. So the correct year on a document is important, and we need to know when the new year begins.

keyTerms.meaning: Legal documents
Loan documents (promissory notes)
Dated earlier than the real date (antedated)
Dated later than the real date (postdated)
Invalid / valid

steps.confusionAlert: Why is a late date allowed? It only works against the lender, who can collect from less property. An early date is what causes harm to innocent buyers.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: For documents.
As we learned: antedated loan documents are invalid,
and postdated ones are valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תשרי New Year is used for dating documents, which must not be antedated.

steps.title: Challenge: רב חסדא already said documents follow ניסן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה already made ניסן the ראש השנה for kings, and רב חסדא explained that this was for documents. So how can תשרי also be for documents?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: the first of ניסן is ראש השנה for kings. We asked what law that was for, and רב חסדא said: for documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא. Documents already have a New Year, ניסן, so it seems they cannot also be the reason for a תשרי New Year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two clauses of the משנה now appear to give the same job to two different dates. If ניסן is for dating documents, then רב פפא's explanation of תשרי seems to contradict it.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Year for counting the years of kings
And we said

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: On the first of Nisan
is the New Year for kings,
and we said: For what law?
and Rav Chisda said: For documents.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: בְּאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לַמְּלָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's answer from Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the תשרי New Year is for documents
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא already gave documents to ניסן, so two different New Years seem to serve the same purpose.

steps.title: Answer: ניסן for Jewish kings, תשרי for non-Jewish kings
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. Documents dated by the reign of Jewish kings count years from ניסן. Documents dated by the reign of non-Jewish kings count years from תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it refers to the kings of Israel, and there it refers to the kings of the nations of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting the cases. Each New Year applies to a different kind of document dating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רב חסדא and רב פפא are correct, but they speak about different documents. Documents dated by Jewish kings change the year in ניסן. Documents dated by non-Jewish kings change the year in תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (there is no contradiction)
Here... there (two different cases)
Jewish kings
Kings of the non-Jewish nations

steps.whatToRemember: Documents dated by Jewish kings count years from ניסן. Documents dated by non-Jewish kings count years from תשרי.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here it refers to the kings of Israel,
phrases.notes: ניסן

phrases.english: there it refers to the kings of the nations of the world.
phrases.notes: תשרי

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן לְמַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, כָּאן לְמַלְכֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both New Years seemed to be for the same documents.
steps.terutzMaskana: ניסן applies to documents dated by Jewish kings, and תשרי to documents dated by non-Jewish kings.

steps.title: Did רב חסדא just repeat the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה's 'תשרי for years' means documents of non-Jewish kings, then רב חסדא's statement adds nothing new.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב חסדא said: 'The משנה's rule of ניסן applies only to Jewish kings. For non-Jewish kings we count from תשרי.' According to what we just said, the משנה already teaches that. Did רב חסדא come just to tell us what the משנה already says?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 20. If the משנה already teaches that non-Jewish kings count from תשרי, then רב חסדא's statement seems useless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 we read 'תשרי for years' as referring to documents dated by non-Jewish kings. But רב חסדא said that same rule as his own new teaching. An אמורא does not normally just repeat a clear משנה, so this reading seems to make his statement unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They only taught this about…', a phrase that limits a משנה to a certain case
Kings of the non-Jewish nations
We count (the years)
He came to teach us

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not challenging the rule itself. It agrees that non-Jewish kings count from תשרי. It only asks why רב חסדא needed to say it.

phrases.english: But that which Rav Chisda said:
They taught this only about the kings of Israel,
but for the kings of the nations of the world
we count from Tishrei,
did Rav Chisda come to teach us the Mishnah?!
phrases.notes: He's not really asking. The point is that an אמורא shouldn't need to repeat a clear משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 20 by showing it makes רב חסדא's statement unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The step 20 reading that 'תשרי for years' refers to documents dated by non-Jewish kings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה already teaches this, רב חסדא's identical statement has no purpose.

steps.title: רב חסדא was explaining פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא was not repeating the משנה. He was teaching how to understand certain פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. רב חסדא came to teach us the meaning of the פסוקים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב חסדא's purpose was to explain פסוקים, not to repeat the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the פרק, the גמרא discussed פסוקים in נחמיה about a non-Jewish king's reign that seemed hard to fit together. רב חסדא's rule, that non-Jewish kings count from תשרי, explains those פסוקים. So the same rule can appear in the משנה and still be useful as the key to reading the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: Verses (פסוקים)

phrases.english: No,
Rav Chisda came to teach us the verses.
phrases.notes: He was explaining פסוקים about non-Jewish kings that were discussed earlier in the פרק.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, רַב חִסְדָּא קְרָאֵי אֲתָא לְאַשְׁמוֹעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the purpose of the אמורא's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא was only restating the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חסדא was using the rule to explain the פסוקים.

steps.title: Second answer: רב חסדא reads the משנה like רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: for רב חסדא, 'תשרי for years' is not about documents at all. It is about the solar cycles (תקופה), following רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: רב חסדא learns the משנה the way רבי זירא does. רבי זירא said 'for years' means for counting the תקופה, the cycles of the sun and moon. This follows רבי אליעזר, who said the world was created in תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. רב חסדא reads 'תשרי for years' as referring to the תקופה, so the משנה never said anything about non-Jewish kings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה's 'for years' is about the solar cycles, it says nothing about documents. Then רב חסדא's rule about non-Jewish kings is completely new. The cycles are counted from תשרי because, according to רבי אליעזר, that is when the world, including the sun and moon, was created.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say', which introduces another answer
The cycle or season of the sun and moon
The world was created

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'ראש השנה for years' can mean different things. Each meaning changes which other statements are new and which are repetitions.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא כְּרַבִּי זֵירָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ.
phrases.english: Rav Chisda learns it like Rabbi Zeira.
For Rabbi Zeira said: it is for the cycle (of sun and moon),
and this follows Rabbi Eliezer,
who said the world was created in Tishrei.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: רַב חִסְדָּא כְּרַבִּי זֵירָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the קשיא of step 21 by changing how the משנה is read.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the משנה so there is no overlap
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'תשרי for years' refers to documents, so it repeats רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב חסדא, 'תשרי for years' refers to the תקופה, so his rule about kings is new.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: תשרי is the New Year for judgment
steps.stepSummary: Another explanation of 'תשרי for years': it is the day of דין, when the world is judged for the whole year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said 'for years' means for judgment. As it says: 'From the beginning of the year until the end of the year.' At the beginning of the year, it is decided what will happen at its end.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives another answer to the question from step 17. He says תשרי is the New Year for judgment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'from the beginning of the year until the end of the year.' רב נחמן בר יצחק reads this to mean that at the start of the year, the whole year's outcome is already decided. That start is the first of תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: Judgment
As it is written
From the beginning of the year
It is judged (decided)

steps.whatToRemember: There are now three meanings of 'תשרי is ראש השנה for years': (1) dating documents of non-Jewish kings, (2) the solar cycles (רבי זירא), and (3) the day of judgment (רב נחמן בר יצחק).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the idea behind ראש השנה as the יום הדין, the day when the coming year is decided.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: לַדִּין,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: it is for judgment,
as it is written: "From the beginning of the year
until the end of the year" (Devarim 11:12),
from the beginning of the year it is decided
what will be at its end.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: לַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to the original question of step 17, alongside רב פפא and רבי זירא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical law does 'the first of תשרי is ראש השנה for years' teach?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the New Year for judgment. On it, the outcome of the whole year is decided.

steps.title: How do we know the day of judgment is in תשרי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the yearly day of judgment falls in תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that the day of judgment is in תשרי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just said that תשרי is the day the world is judged. Now it asks for the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 explained 'תשרי for years' as the day of דין. A claim like this needs a source, so the גמרא asks what tells us the judgment happens in תשרי and not in some other month.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? (Asking for a source)
The month of תשרי, in the autumn
The day of judgment, when the world is judged for the year

phrases.english: From where do we know that it is Tishrei?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the day of judgment mentioned in the previous step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source behind Step 24's claim that the day of judgment is in תשרי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that the yearly judgment takes place in תשרי.

steps.title: The verse about blowing the שופר on the covered festival day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק 'Blow the שופר at the new moon, at the covered time, for our festival day', and asks which festival this is.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Blow the שופר at the new moon, at the covered time, for our festival day.' Which festival is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer with a פסוק from תהילים. It then asks 'which festival is it?', which sets up the next part of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about a festival that falls בַּכֵּסֶה, when the moon is 'covered', which means the start of a month when the moon cannot be seen. The גמרא asks which festival falls on the first day of a month. Identifying it will show that the judgment day, marked by the שופר, is in תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)
Blow the שופר at the new moon
At the covered time, when the moon is hidden at the start of the month
Which festival is it?

steps.confusionAlert: בַּכֵּסֶה does not mean 'at the set time' here. The גמרא reads it as 'covered', meaning the day the moon is hidden. That is the first day of a month.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Blow a shofar at the new moon
phrases.notes: תהילים פא:ד

phrases.english: at the covered time, for our festival day'

phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud. The גמרא is about to identify the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: תִּקְעוּ בַחֹדֶשׁ שׁוֹפָר בַּכֵּסֶה לְיוֹם חַגֵּנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering Step 25 by bringing a פסוק, then asks a guiding question to identify the festival.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק in תהילים about blowing the שופר on a festival that falls on the 'covered' day of the month. The full identification of the festival continues on the next amud.
